reason: The bent antenna seems the direct obstacle to getting the radio working, and the tool may straighten it.
expectation: I expect a repaired or freed antenna, though it may still need mounting.

alternatives.reason: The foil and felt may insulate the window, but I want to address the radio first.

effect: The antenna is straightened, so mounting it is the next apparent radio step.
reaction: That worked as expected; the result is clear but brief.
reason: Mounting the antenna should connect it to the radio installation.
expectation: I expect the antenna to be fitted and perhaps the radio to work, although it might need power too.

effect: The radio works after mounting the antenna, so I can turn to the cabin's heat loss.
reaction: The twelve-minute-old voice makes the distance from Earth feel tangible, and I am curious about the reply.
reason: Foil and felt look like materials for a window insulation layer.
expectation: I expect an insulating panel or curtain, probably needing attachment at the window.

alternatives.reason: Charging the emergency battery also seems useful for night, but I want to fix the window first.

effect: The materials made quilt stock, and the offered window action suggests fitting it there next.
reaction: The result makes sense, though I am unsure what role the spare rail will play.
reason: The window is losing heat and the quilt looks intended to cover it.
expectation: I expect a window covering, possibly needing the rail to complete it.

effect: The quilt is at the window, and the rail is now compatible with it.
reaction: That answers my question about the rail; the sequence feels practical.
reason: The rail should make the quilt usable as a movable window covering.
expectation: I expect the quilt to hang from the rail and help retain heat.

effect: The quilt slides and eases the cold, but the night goal remains incomplete; charging the battery is the remaining action.
reaction: I like the concrete sensation of less cold and being able to see the plain again in the morning.
reason: Charge the emergency battery as the only available gameplay action and prepare for night.
expectation: I expect a charged backup battery and the night goal to complete.

effect: Charging the battery completed the night goal, and I understand there is also a supplied fuel-cell backup for essential systems.
reaction: The connection to the recovered array makes the earlier work feel useful, although the backup detail arrives quickly.

mostWorthwhile.text: The recorded voice made the communication delay personal and gave the repair an emotional payoff.

leastWorthwhile.text: Straightening the antenna produced only a terse item name; it felt like a necessary but mechanically thin step.

surprise.text: The message was already twelve minutes old, making the delay tangible; the supplied fuel-cell backup was also new information.

arbitrary.text: None felt purposeless: the rail, initially unexplained, became a plausible sliding curtain support. The separate quilt placement and rail fitting were slightly procedural.

continue.text: Yes. The voice and view of the plain make me curious about the expedition, though I hope later construction offers more consequential decisions than choosing the order of obvious repairs.
